question.knowledge_point: Applying Row Operations To a Coefficients Matrix
question.problem:
Consider the matrix $C,$ given by

$$
C=[\begin{aligned}9 & 6 & -7 \\ 1 & -3 & -2 \\ -2 & 4 & -3\end{aligned}].
$$

What matrix results from carrying out the following row operations on $C?$

$$
\begin{aligned}{R}_{2} & :={R}_{2}+3{R}_{1} \\ {R}_{2} & :={R}_{2}-{R}_{3}\end{aligned}
$$
question.worked_solution:
Let's list the required operations:

- The operation ${R}_{2}:={R}_{2}+3{R}_{1}$ means that we need to add $3$ times the first row to the second row.

- The operation ${R}_{2}:={R}_{2}-{R}_{3}$ means that we need to add $-1$ times the third row to the second row.

Applying the operations, we obtain the following:

$$
\begin{aligned}C & =[\begin{aligned}9 & 6 & -7 \\ 1 & -3 & -2 \\ -2 & 4 & -3\end{aligned}]\,{R}_{2}:={R}_{2}+3\cdot {R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}9 & 6 & -7 \\ 1+(3)(9) & -3+(3)(6) & -2+(3)(-7) \\ -2 & 4 & -3\end{aligned}] \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}9 & 6 & -7 \\ 28 & 15 & -23 \\ -2 & 4 & -3\end{aligned}]\,{R}_{2}:={R}_{2}+(-1)\cdot {R}_{3} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}9 & 6 & -7 \\ 28+(-1)(-2) & 15+(-1)(4) & -23+(-1)(-3) \\ -2 & 4 & -3\end{aligned}] \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}9 & 6 & -7 \\ 30 & 11 & -20 \\ -2 & 4 & -3\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

question.knowledge_point: Applying Row Operations To a Coefficients Matrix
question.problem:
Consider the matrix $M,$ given by

$$
M=[\begin{aligned}-1 & 2 & 4 \\ 8 & 3 & 1 \\ 3 & -1 & 9\end{aligned}].
$$

What matrix results from carrying out the row operation ${R}_{3}:={R}_{3}+3{R}_{1}$ on $M?$
question.worked_solution:
The operation ${R}_{3}:={R}_{3}+3{R}_{1}$ means that we need to add $3$ times the first row to the third row.

Applying this row operation, we obtain the following:

$$
\begin{aligned}M & =[\begin{aligned}-1 & 2 & 4 \\ 8 & 3 & 1 \\ 3 & -1 & 9\end{aligned}]\,{R}_{3}:={R}_{3}+3\cdot {R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & -2 & -4 \\ 8 & 3 & 1 \\ 3+(3)(-1) & -1+(3)(2) & 9+(3)(4)\end{aligned}] \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}-1 & 2 & 4 \\ 8 & 3 & 1 \\ 0 & 5 & 21\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

question.knowledge_point: Applying Row Operations To an Augmented Matrix
question.problem:
Consider the augmented matrix $N,$ given by

$$
N=[\begin{aligned}1 & -2 & 1 & -1 \\ 2 & 1 & 2 & 3 \\ 7 & -1 & 3 & 1\end{aligned}].
$$

What matrix results from carrying out the row operation ${R}_{2}:={R}_{2}+(-2)\cdot {R}_{1}$ on $N?$
question.worked_solution:
The operation ${R}_{2}:={R}_{2}+(-2)\cdot {R}_{1}$ means that we need to add $-2$ times the first row to the second row.

Applying this row operation, we obtain the following:

$$
\begin{aligned}N & =[\begin{aligned}1 & -2 & 1 & -1 \\ 2 & 1 & 2 & 3 \\ 7 & -1 & 3 & 1\end{aligned}]\,{R}_{2}:={R}_{2}+(-2)\cdot {R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & -2 & 1 & -1 \\ 2+(-2)(1) & 1+(-2)(-2) & 2+(-2)(1) & 3+(-2)(-1) \\ 7 & -1 & 3 & 1\end{aligned}] \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & -2 & 1 & -1 \\ 0 & 5 & 0 & 5 \\ 7 & -1 & 3 & 1\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

question.knowledge_point: Applying Row Operations To an Augmented Matrix
question.problem:
Consider the augmented matrix $T,$ given by

$$
T=[\begin{aligned}1 & 3 & 2 \\ -2 & -2 & 1\end{aligned}].
$$

What matrix results from carrying out the row operation ${R}_{2}:={R}_{2}+2{R}_{1}$ on $T?$
question.worked_solution:
The operation ${R}_{2}:={R}_{2}+2{R}_{1}$ means that we need to add $2$ times the first row to the second row. 

Applying this row operation, we obtain the following:  

$$
\begin{aligned}T & =[\begin{aligned}1 & 3 & 2 \\ -2 & -2 & 1\end{aligned}]\,{R}_{2}:={R}_{2}+2\cdot {R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 3 & 2 \\ -2+(2)(1) & -2+(2)(3) & 1+(2)(2)\end{aligned}] \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 3 & 2 \\ 0 & 4 & 5\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

question.knowledge_point: Identifying the Appropriate Row Operation To Transform One Matrix Into Another
question.problem:
Which of the following elementary row operations transforms the matrix $S$ into the matrix $T$, where

$$
S=[\begin{aligned}60 & 0 & 120 \\ 20 & 0 & 40 \\ 15 & 0 & 30\end{aligned}],\,T=[\begin{aligned}15 & 0 & 30 \\ 20 & 0 & 40 \\ 15 & 0 & 30\end{aligned}]?
$$
question.worked_solution:
First, notice that the $2$nd and $3$rd rows are the same in both matrices. The only row that has changed is the $1$st row. 

By considering the given row operations that changes the $1$st  row, we notice that

$$
\begin{aligned}S & =[\begin{aligned}60 & 0 & 120 \\ 20 & 0 & 40 \\ 15 & 0 & 30\end{aligned}] & \,{R}_{1}:=\frac{1}{4}\cdot {R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}15 & 0 & 30 \\ 20 & 0 & 40 \\ 15 & 0 & 30\end{aligned}] \\  & =T.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the required row operation is

$$
{R}_{1}:=\frac{1}{4}{R}_{1}.
$$

provenance.kp_title: Identifying the Appropriate Row Operation To Transform One Matrix Into Another

question.knowledge_point: Identifying the Appropriate Row Operation To Transform One Matrix Into Another
question.problem:
Which of the following elementary row operations transforms the matrix $X$ into the matrix $W$, where

$$
X=[\begin{aligned}1 & 1 & 2 \\ -4 & -1 & 1 \\ 2 & 1 & 6\end{aligned}],\,W=[\begin{aligned}1 & 1 & 2 \\ 0 & 3 & 9 \\ 2 & 1 & 6\end{aligned}]?
$$
question.worked_solution:
First, notice that the $1$st and the $3$rd rows are the same in both matrices. The only row that has changed is the $2$nd row. 

By considering the given row operations that modify the $2$nd row, we notice that

$$
\begin{aligned}X & =[\begin{aligned}1 & 1 & 2 \\ -4 & -1 & 1 \\ 2 & 1 & 6\end{aligned}]\,{R}_{2}:={R}_{2}+4\cdot {R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 1 & 2 \\ 0 & 3 & 9 \\ 2 & 1 & 6\end{aligned}] \\  & =W.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the required row operation is

$$
{R}_{2}:={R}_{2}+4{R}_{1}.
$$

question.knowledge_point: Identifying the Appropriate Row Operation To Transform a Given Entry to a Desired Value
question.problem:
Given that
$S=[\begin{aligned}1 & -1 & 1 \\ 3 & 2 & 1 \\ 1 & 1 & 3\end{aligned}]$,
which of the following elementary row operations makes ${a}_{33}=0?$
question.worked_solution:
Of the given options, we consider the row operation 

$$
{R}_{3}:={R}_{3}-3{R}_{1}={R}_{3}+(-3)\cdot {R}_{1}
$$

Applying the above row operation, we obtain the following:

$$
\begin{aligned}S & =[\begin{aligned}1 & -1 & 1 \\ 3 & 2 & 1 \\ 1 & 1 & 3\end{aligned}]\,{R}_{3}:={R}_{3}+(-3)\cdot {R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & -1 & 1 \\ 3 & 2 & 1 \\ -2 & 4 & 0\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the required row operation is 

$$
{R}_{3}:={R}_{3}+(-3)\cdot {R}_{1}
$$

or simply

$$
{R}_{3}:={R}_{3}-3{R}_{1}.
$$

question.problem:
Given 
$A=[\begin{aligned}6 & 2 & 4 \\ -9 & 1 & -5 \\ 8 & 4 & 0\end{aligned}]$,
which of the following elementary row operations makes ${a}_{32}=0?$
question.worked_solution:
Of the given options, we consider the row operation 

$$
{R}_{3}:={R}_{3}+(-2){R}_{1}.
$$

Applying the above row operation, we obtain the following:

$$
\begin{aligned}A & =[\begin{aligned}6 & 2 & 4 \\ -9 & 1 & -5 \\ 8 & 4 & 0\end{aligned}]\,{R}_{3}:={R}_{3}+(-2)\cdot {R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}6 & 2 & 4 \\ -9 & 1 & -5 \\ -4 & 0 & -8\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

 

Therefore, the required row operation is

$$
{R}_{3}:={R}_{3}+(-2){R}_{1}.
$$

question.knowledge_point: Finding the Complement of a Set Using a Venn Diagram
question.problem:
![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture/14071504/assets/02dabe7099c201f717885a05842e0cb8543bd01cccf0d6c52147f674cde15dce.png)

Let $U=\{a,b,c,20,40\}$ be the universal set and let $R=\{b,20,40\}.$ What is the complement of $R?$
question.worked_solution:
The complement of $R,$ denoted $\overset{―}{R},$ consists of all the elements in $U$ that are not in $R.$ To represent $\overset{―}{R},$ we will shade in all the area of $U$ that is *outside* of $R,$ as follows:

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture/14071504/assets/79900f22c35570b35cf10664768ecf4460a7953ddf7f91dac1893b3ce81339bf.png)

The elements in the shaded area are $a$ and $c.$ These are the elements of $U$ that are not in $R.$ Therefore, the complement of $R$ is

$$
\overset{―}{R}=\{a,c\}.
$$

provenance.kp_title: Finding the Complement of a Set Using a Venn Diagram

question.knowledge_point: Finding the Complement of a Set Given Using Ellipsis Notation
question.worked_solution:
The complement of $A,$ denoted $\overset{―}{A},$ consists of every element in the universal set $U$ that is not in the set $A.$

The universal set $U$ consists of the even integers $-20$ through $20,$ while the set $A$ consists of the multiples of $4$ from $-20$ through $20.$

So, the only elements of $U$ that are not in $A$ are the even integers from $-18$ through $18$ that are not multiples of $4.$

Therefore, the complement of $A$ is

$$
\overset{―}{A}=\{-18,-14,-10,-6,-2,2,6,10,14,18\}.
$$

question.knowledge_point: Identifying the Leading Entries of a Matrix
question.problem:
What is the sum of the leading entries of the $1$st and $4$th rows in the matrix $A,$ given below?

$$
A=[\begin{aligned}0 & 0 & 1 & 3 \\ 4 & 3 & 0 & 0 \\ -2 & 0 & -1 & 8 \\ 0 & -3 & 0 & 2\end{aligned}]
$$
question.worked_solution:
The first non-zero entry of each row (from left to right) is the leading entry. 

Therefore, the leading entries of the $1$st and $4$th rows of $A$ are $1$ and $-3$, respectively.

$$
A=[\begin{aligned}0 & 0 & 1 & 3 \\ 4 & 3 & 0 & 0 \\ -2 & 0 & -1 & 8 \\ 0 & -3 & 0 & 2\end{aligned}]
$$

So, the answer is $1+(-3)=-2.$

provenance.kp_title: Identifying the Leading Entries of a Matrix

question.knowledge_point: Identifying the Leading Entries of a Matrix
question.problem:
What is the sum of the leading entries of the $1$st, $2$nd, and $3$rd rows in the matrix $A,$ given below?

$$
A=[\begin{aligned}0 & -7 & 2 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 5 & 6 \\ 3 & 0 & 2 & -1 \\ -1 & 0 & 0 & 1\end{aligned}]
$$
question.worked_solution:
The first non-zero entry of each row (from left to right) is the leading entry. 

Therefore, the leading entries of the $1$st, $2$nd, and $3$rd rows of $A$ are $-7$, $5$, and $3$, respectively.

$$
A=[\begin{aligned}0 & -7 & 2 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 5 & 6 \\ 3 & 0 & 2 & -1 \\ -1 & 0 & 0 & 1\end{aligned}]
$$

So, the answer is $-7+5+3=1.$
